frame: Who: every seller. Carol (clearing out) opens it when the inbox shows a count; a flipper opens it many times a day.
Came to: see who wrote, about which thing, and open the one to answer, without opening five apps.
A mistake costs most where an offer runs out unseen, or where a scammer gets an answer: the scam row says so in its one word, and Today holds every decision with its deadline.
Ways out (spec/ways-out.md §6.3): show one item's messages (?item=); a blocked buyer stays in the list as Blocked; Ask me first and Take over live in the conversation.
In the loop: replies start as drafts (ways-out §6.3). A row with one says Draft ready; the draft is sent, edited or taken over inside the conversation, next to the words it answers.

decisions.decision: The page is the list and nothing else: a back arrow, the large title, one row per conversation
decisions.why: Ben, 09:56: "messages should just list the messages"; iOS Messages and Mail open this way (10:01, "standard to apple iphone design").

decisions.decision: The drafts queue, Send all and the inline Send, Edit and Take over left the list
decisions.why: A draft is answered next to the buyer's words, in the conversation, where it already has Send, Edit and Take over; on the list it put a second page and four buttons above the rows.

decisions.decision: A row with a draft says Draft ready, quietly, as Mail marks a Draft
decisions.why: The person sees where a reply waits without a colored tag on every row (Art. 7.14).

decisions.decision: The state tags (Offer, Reply, Pickup) left the rows; Possible scam stays, as one word with its icon in brick
decisions.why: Today already holds every decision; a scam is the one a person must not miss on the list (copy.md, safety copy is the exception).

decisions.decision: Each row is who and the time, the thing's short name, their last words and the count
decisions.why: Mail's sender, subject and preview: a buyer's name alone means nothing, the thing tells which conversation it is (brief, Art. 7.15).

decisions.decision: Each row carries the site's square logo on the item's photo
decisions.why: The photo says which thing, the logo which site; a site's name is never written as words (kit, SiteBadge).

decisions.decision: An unread count, not a dot; the last words stay in the second ink
decisions.why: It matches the count on the inbox in every tab's title row; one mark for unread is enough, and three levels (who at 18, the thing at 15 in ink, their words at 15 in the second ink) are Mail's sender, subject and preview.

decisions.decision: Every site in one list, newest first
decisions.why: Mail and iMessage order an inbox this way, and decision "All messages live behind a chat icon with a count" puts every site here.

decisions.decision: The filter button and its sheet of items went; ?item= still shows one thing's conversations
decisions.why: No world holds more than five conversations, so the filter cost a control and a sheet for nothing; a thing's page can link straight to its own.

decisions.decision: The "sent for you this week" line went; a row whose last message the agent sent says Sent for you
decisions.why: What the agent did stays visible on the row it did it in, and its why and Ask me first are one tap away in the conversation.

five conversations across sites, two with a draft ready, one flagged as a possible scam

skips.loading: a thread row has no skeleton in the kit yet, and a card skeleton would move the list when it lands
skips.dense: no world holds more than five conversations, and a longer list is the same rows
